title: Why Iran Won’t Change
gist: Truncated commentary opening: Banihashemi argues a doctrine embedded in the Islamic Republic's foundations licenses total repression and the mobilization of all state resources to preserve the system, which is why US and Israeli expectations of behavioral change or popular overthrow were misplaced. Context given: Khamenei was killed in the opening wave of US-Israeli airstrikes in February 2026, and executions of protesters and political prisoners have accelerated through his funeral and renewed bombardment.

insights.claim: A doctrine embedded in the Islamic Republic's foundations permits total repression of the population and the mobilization of all state resources to preserve the system, making regime behavioral change or collapse-by-uprising structurally unlikely.
insights.speaker: Pegah Banihashemi
insights.so_what: Rules out the fast-resolution scenarios in Iran risk models — price persistent sanctions, persistent conflict risk and no near-term political normalization.
insights.quote: Embedded in the Islamic Republic’s foundations is a doctrine that allows for total repression of the population and mobilization of all state resources to preserve the system.
insights.locator: Embedded in the Islamic Republic's foundations

insights.claim: The US and Israel were wrong to expect that military pressure would change the Iranian regime's behavior, let alone bring it down via the Iranian people.
insights.speaker: Pegah Banihashemi
insights.so_what: Directly contradicts the coercion-works premise behind the strike campaign — implies a longer conflict tail and sustained Middle East energy risk premium.
insights.locator: This helps to explain why the US and Israel were wrong

insights.claim: Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed in the opening wave of US-Israeli airstrikes in February 2026, and bombardment of Iran's south continued through and after his funeral.
insights.speaker: Pegah Banihashemi
insights.so_what: Decapitation of the supreme leadership did not end the campaign or the state — a live conflict with no obvious termination point for regional risk pricing.
insights.locator: CHICAGO—As the funeral of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei

insights.claim: Through the funeral rites and renewed airstrikes alike, the one Iranian state institution that never broke its stride was the gallows, with recently seized protesters and long-held political prisoners being executed at a rapid rate.
insights.speaker: Pegah Banihashemi
insights.so_what: Repression capacity surviving intact after leadership decapitation is the clearest observable evidence against the internal-collapse thesis.
insights.quote: one state institution never broke its stride: the gallows
